snp3.11:1.2: Reading Sakkañca with the Thai edition.
snp3.11:25.4: For an instance of a woman who tried to seduce a monk, see the origin story to Pācittiya 5 in The Buddhist Monastic Code, volume 1; for an instance of a man who tried to seduce a nun, see Thig 14.
snp3.11:36.4: According to SnA, the high and low practices the Buddha teaches are, respectively, the mode of pleasant practice with quick intuition, and the mode of painful practice with slow intuition (see AN 4:162). These modes “don’t go twice to the further shore” in the sense that each of the four paths—to stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arahantship—abandons whatever defilements it can abandon once and for all, with no need to repeat that particular path. Unbinding “isn’t sensed only once” in the sense that it’s touched anew as the result of each of the four paths.
snp3.11:37.2: SnA glosses this as the stream of defilements, though it could also be the stream of becoming mentioned at Sn 3:12.
snp3.11:43.4: This verse is quoted in the Milinda Pañhā.
